step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified user entry point indicated by the squiggly arrow on the left pointing to Route 53.
2. Identified Route 53 service node.
3. Identified the Front End path: Route 53 -> ALB (Front End) -> ECS (Front End) -> Route 53 (loop back to backend domain).
4. Identified the Back End path: Route 53 -> ALB (Back End) -> ECS (Back End).
5. From ECS (Back End), connections go to Aurora MySQL for database storage and Amazon MQ for message processing.
6. Identified DMS (Database Migration Service) feeding data into Aurora MySQL.
7. Identified the drawn cyan line connecting Route 53 and DMS.

edges.notes: Route 53 directs front-end traffic to Front End ALB
Front End ALB forwards to Front End ECS
Front End ECS calls back-end via Route 53 DNS query
Route 53 routes back-end request to Back End ALB
Back End ALB forwards request to Back End ECS
Back End ECS reads/writes to Aurora MySQL
Back End ECS generates/consumes messages with Amazon MQ
DMS migrates data into Aurora MySQL
Blue line drawn connecting DMS back across to Route 53
